model.note: Mentions are evidence, not edges. Constraints are node attributes.

nodes.label: adk-agent-builder
nodes.description: Builds ADK (Agent Development Kit) Python agents: LLM agents with tools, graph workflows of function and agent nodes, conditional routing, fan-out and join, schema-validated delegation between agents, human-in-the-loop pauses, and pytest coverage for all of it. Use when asked to create an agent or a workflow, add a tool to one, branch or loop between nodes, run steps in parallel, pause for user approval, or test an agent. Don't use for explaining how ADK works internally or designing its core components (use `adk-architecture`), for an agent that already runs but misbehaves (use `adk-debug`), for authoring a sample under `contributing/` (use `adk-sample-creator`), or for naming, typing, and formatting conventions (use `adk-style`).

nodes.label: adk-architecture
nodes.description: Explains how the ADK runtime fits together: the node and graph execution model, Context and Event flow, checkpoint and resume, tracing, and the rules governing the public API surface. Use when answering "how does X work" about ADK internals, tracing where an event or a piece of state comes from, deciding where a new capability belongs, reviewing a change to BaseNode, Workflow, Runner, Agent, Event or Context, working out why a node re-ran or stayed waiting after a resume, or judging whether a change breaks the public API. Don't use for assembling an agent from existing pieces (use adk-agent-builder), diagnosing one failing run or test (use adk-debug), or formatting and naming conventions (use adk-style).

nodes.label: adk-debug
nodes.description: Diagnoses misbehaving ADK agents by inspecting sessions, events, tool calls, and the exact request that reached the model. Covers the `adk run` CLI and the `adk web` dev server with its session, trace, and debug HTTP endpoints. Use when an agent returns the wrong answer, ignores a tool or swallows a tool error, hangs, loops, emits raw JSON instead of calling tools, is not discovered by `adk web`, when a sub-agent cannot see the parent conversation, or when you need the LLM request/response, token counts, or logs for a run. Don't use for how ADK is designed internally (use `adk-architecture`), for building a new agent or workflow (use `adk-agent-builder`), for environment or dependency setup failures (use `adk-setup`), or for lint and style nits (use `adk-style`).

nodes.label: adk-git
nodes.description: Writes commit messages and pull request descriptions for the adk-python repository: Conventional Commits types and scopes, subject lines that say why a change was made, and the linked-issue and testing-plan sections the PR template requires. Use when writing or rewording a commit message, squashing commits before a pull request, drafting a PR description, or checking that a change is shaped to land. Don't use for generic git mechanics such as rebasing, resolving conflicts, cherry-picking, or branch surgery; those need no skill. Don't use to judge the content of a change (use adk-review) or for code style and naming (use adk-style).

nodes.label: adk-review
nodes.description: Reviews the uncommitted changes in an adk-python working tree and reports correctness, design, public-API stability, test, sample and documentation gaps as a prioritized findings report, fixing them only when asked. Use when the user asks to review local changes, wants a self-review before opening a pull request, asks whether a change breaks the public API or needs tests, samples or docs, or asks what is wrong with the current diff. Required for changes to public APIs, core architecture (Runner, Workflow, BaseNode), new features and major refactors. Don't use for a single style nit (use adk-style), for diagnosing a failing test or a misbehaving agent at runtime (use adk-debug), or for wording a commit message or PR description (use adk-git).

nodes.label: adk-sample-creator
nodes.description: Creates a new sample agent in the ADK Python repository — the sample directory, its `agent.py`, and its `README.md` — following the conventions the existing samples already use. Use when the user wants to add a sample or example demonstrating a feature or agent pattern (dynamic nodes, fan-out/fan-in, a standalone tool-using agent), asks where a new sample belongs under `contributing/samples/`, or wants an existing sample's README brought up to the standard structure. Don't use for building a real working agent for the user's own project (use `adk-agent-builder`), or for checking whether the Python blocks in a Markdown file run (use `adk-verify-snippets`).

nodes.label: adk-setup
nodes.description: Sets up a local ADK Python development environment in a git clone of the open-source adk-python repository: a uv virtual environment, all dependency extras, pre-commit hooks, and a first unit-test run. Runs only when explicitly requested, never on its own. Use when asked to set up, bootstrap, or repair a development checkout, install project dependencies, fix a missing or broken .venv, or prepare a machine for contributing a pull request. Don't use for debugging a running agent (use adk-debug), for commit and pull-request mechanics (use adk-git), or for re-running formatters on a checkout that is already set up (pre-commit run --all-files).

nodes.label: adk-style
nodes.description: Python style and codebase conventions for ADK (Agent Development Kit): private-by-default file visibility, imports, type hints, Pydantic v2 models, formatting, docstrings, logging, async I/O, file and test layout, and unit test structure. Use when writing or editing ADK source or tests, deciding whether a new file or symbol should be public or private, naming or placing a test file, fixing a formatter, linter, or type-check failure (pyink, isort, ruff, mypy, addlicense, compliance-checks), or asking whether code matches house style. Don't use for reviewing a whole changeset (use adk-review), writing a developer guide or design doc for a code unit (use adk-unit-guide or adk-unit-design), building or configuring agents (use adk-agent-builder), or installing the toolchain (use adk-setup).

nodes.label: adk-unit-design
nodes.description: Writes an as-built architecture document for one ADK code unit — purpose, execution flow, data flow, cross-class dependencies, extension points, and the parts that must not change — to `docs/design/{topic}/{unit}/index.md`. It describes the code as implemented, not a proposed design, and its reader is a developer about to change or extend that unit. Use when asked to "write a design doc for {file}", "document the architecture of {class}", "document the extension points of {unit}", or after adding a core class, node type, or plugin base. Don't use for documentation aimed at developers who only call the unit from their own application — that is a usage guide with runnable examples under `docs/guides/` (use `adk-unit-guide`). Don't use to answer a framework-wide architecture question (use `adk-architecture`).

nodes.label: adk-unit-guide
nodes.description: Writes a hands-on developer guide for one ADK code unit — a minimal runnable example, how it works, a configuration-option table, advanced uses, limitations, and links to related samples — to `docs/guides/{topic}/{unit}/index.md`, then lists it in the index at `docs/guides/README.md`. Its reader is a developer calling the unit from their own application, at more depth than the published adk.dev documentation carries. Use when asked to "write a unit guide for {class}", "document how to use {feature}", "add a guide for {file}", or after shipping a user-facing class, node, or plugin. Don't use for internals documentation aimed at someone changing or extending the unit — that is a design document under `docs/design/` (use `adk-unit-design`). Don't use to write a runnable sample under `contributing/samples/` (use `adk-sample-creator`).

nodes.label: adk-verify-snippets
nodes.description: Checks that every Python code block in a Markdown file actually compiles and runs, by extracting each block to a temporary file, executing it in an isolated subprocess, and writing a pass/fail report with per-snippet coverage. Use when the user asks to verify, test, or validate the code samples in a README, a guide, or a documentation page; wants to know which snippets in a Markdown file are broken or out of date; or asks for a snippet verification report. Don't use for running the project's test suite (run pytest directly), for checking code style or formatting (use `adk-style`), or for authoring a new runnable sample agent (use `adk-sample-creator`).

nodes.label: ai-development
nodes.description: Design, build and operate AI-enabled applications and agent integrations independently of a provider. Use for model/tool workflows, context and retrieval, skills, harnesses, MCP, agent interaction or generated UI, and their evaluation and delivery; apply technical guidance only to the accepted stack.

nodes.label: ai-evaluation
nodes.description: Plan, run and report a program-level AI evaluation for a change, release or product claim. Use for acceptance criteria, dataset and slice governance, grader choice and calibration, baselines, experiments, CI gates, production sampling, regression and red-team coverage, and the evidence behind a go/no-go recommendation.

nodes.label: ai-operations
nodes.description: Define and improve AI operating behavior across task observability, quality monitoring, latency/cost, provider limits, drift, rollout and recovery. Use for AI production readiness, operational diagnosis or learning from live behavior independently of a language, telemetry SDK or monitoring backend.

nodes.label: ai-testing
nodes.description: Design and assess AI testing and evaluation across components, retrieval, agent trajectories, conversations, protocols and product journeys. Use for quality criteria, datasets, graders, regression gates and evaluation evidence independently of an implementation library or application language.

nodes.label: langchain-dependencies
nodes.description: INVOKE THIS SKILL when setting up a new project or when asked about package versions, installation, or dependency management for LangChain, LangGraph, LangSmith, or Deep Agents. Covers required packages, minimum versions, environment requirements, versioning best practices, and common community tool packages for both Python and TypeScript.

nodes.label: langchain-fundamentals
nodes.description: Create LangChain agents with create_agent, define tools, and use middleware for human-in-the-loop and error handling.

nodes.label: langgraph-fundamentals
nodes.description: INVOKE THIS SKILL when writing ANY LangGraph code. Covers StateGraph, state schemas, nodes, edges, Command, Send, invoke, streaming, and error handling.

nodes.label: langgraph-persistence
nodes.description: INVOKE THIS SKILL when your LangGraph needs to persist state, remember conversations, travel through history, or configure subgraph checkpointer scoping. Covers checkpointers, thread_id, time travel, Store, and subgraph persistence modes.

nodes.label: ai-conventions
nodes.description: Implement accepted Python model/provider adapters and standalone FastMCP interfaces. Use for Gemini integration, version-matched Python MCP APIs and interaction integration; preserve established providers and frameworks.

nodes.label: ai-deepeval-testing
nodes.description: Implement Python AI evaluation suites with DeepEval for model, retrieval, agent trajectory, conversation and end-to-end quality. Use when DeepEval is selected or being evaluated; preserve existing evaluation tools and do not introduce model calls, hosted reporting or synthetic generation without scope.

nodes.label: mcp-builder
nodes.description: Guide for creating high-quality MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that enable LLMs to interact with external services through well-designed tools. Use when building MCP servers to integrate external APIs or services, whether in Python (FastMCP) or Node/TypeScript (MCP SDK).

nodes.label: python-ai-observability
nodes.description: Set up and verify Python AI observability with OpenTelemetry and compatible model/framework instrumentation. Use for AI task/tool/retrieval traces, usage and latency signals, export/privacy configuration and operational diagnosis; keep the chosen backend and quality evaluation separate.

nodes.label: architecture-patterns
nodes.description: Select and compare backend architecture patterns — modular monolith, layered, hexagonal/ports-and-adapters, clean/onion, CQRS, event sourcing, microservices and serverless — by the forces that justify them, their costs and migration path. Use when an architecture proposal or option comparison needs pattern candidates, a fit check or a tradeoff review; the architecture decision, service behavior, event contracts and cross-service failure reasoning stay with their owning capabilities.

nodes.label: backend-design
nodes.description: Define application-service behavior, authority, state and interface contracts independently of a framework. Use for APIs, durable jobs, stored data or integration changes before dependent implementation; preserve accepted behavior for local fixes.

nodes.label: distributed-systems
nodes.description: Reason about cross-service consistency, replication, partitioning, consensus, time, failure detection, retries, timeouts, circuit breakers, idempotency, ambiguous outcomes, multi-region recovery and capacity. Use when a design or incident depends on behavior across process, network or region boundaries; architecture decisions, service contracts, fault experiments and telemetry stay with their owning activities.

nodes.label: event-driven-design
nodes.description: Design event and message contracts across services, including event meaning, schema evolution, ordering and partitioning, delivery and idempotency, replay, retention and failure handling. Use when a change publishes or consumes events, introduces asynchronous integration or alters an existing event contract; not for broker installation or cluster operations.

nodes.label: graphql-design
nodes.description: Design a GraphQL schema and API contract covering domain types, nullability, connections, errors, mutations, idempotency, N+1 and cost limits, field authorization, persisted queries, federation boundaries, deprecation, caching and public versus private surfaces. Use before implementing resolvers or changing a schema; not for resolver code or service behavior design.

nodes.label: rest-api-design
nodes.description: Design a REST/HTTP API contract covering resources, method and status semantics, representations, errors, collections, idempotency, conditional requests, versioning, caching, authorization boundaries, rate limits and OpenAPI. Use before implementing or changing an HTTP interface; not for service behavior design or framework setup.

nodes.label: backend-conventions
nodes.description: Build, extend or review Python/FastAPI systems with SQLAlchemy, Alembic, contextual persistence, auth, API contracts, jobs and optional AI/FastMCP. Use for backend architecture, endpoints, migrations, transactions, integrations and verification; accept reference systems and preserve established project constraints.

nodes.label: modern-python
nodes.description: Configures Python projects with modern tooling (uv, ruff, ty). Use when creating projects, writing standalone scripts, or migrating from pip/Poetry/mypy/black.

nodes.label: python-automation-engineering
nodes.description: Design, implement, review and maintain useful Python operational automations and reporting tools with ergonomic CLIs, typed boundaries, reproducible projects, complete API collection, resumable mutations and verified outcomes.

nodes.label: browser-extension-delivery
nodes.description: Prepare or review Chrome MV3 release packages and Chrome Web Store readiness. Use for production ZIP contents, listing/privacy evidence, update compatibility and authorized upload/submission/publication; preserve existing CI and release policy.

nodes.label: browser-extension-development
nodes.description: Design, implement, debug or migrate Chrome Manifest V3 extensions. Use for extension entrypoints, background lifecycle, messaging, persistence and WXT/CRXJS integration; preserve the accepted UI framework and backend.

nodes.label: browser-extension-security
nodes.description: Design, implement or review Chrome MV3 permissions and extension trust boundaries. Use for manifest grants, content-script messaging, privileged fetch/injection, extension storage and browser-to-backend identity.

nodes.label: browser-extension-testing
nodes.description: Plan and execute Chrome MV3 unit, component and real-extension tests. Use for worker restart, popup/panel lifecycle, site permissions, messaging and production-package verification with a compatible browser driver.

nodes.label: browser-extension-ui
nodes.description: Design, implement or assess Chrome extension experiences by matching user tasks to suitable UI patterns and browser surfaces. Use for extension information architecture, surface lifecycle, injected UI, permission states and assets; preserve the product's design system.

nodes.label: database-design
nodes.description: Design or evolve stored data, constraints, transactions and migration behavior independently of a database engine. Use for persistence choices, schema changes, consistency boundaries and data lifecycle decisions.

nodes.label: database-performance
nodes.description: Investigate database workload performance and compare improvements while preserving correctness and operating budgets. Use for latency, throughput, contention, connection or resource bottlenecks before choosing engine-specific tuning.

nodes.label: postgresql-development
nodes.description: Develop or review PostgreSQL schemas, transactions, migrations and access policies. Use for SQL, data integrity, concurrency and engine-specific persistence behavior with the actual application roles and server version.

nodes.label: postgresql-operations
nodes.description: Plan or perform scoped PostgreSQL backup/recovery, maintenance, replication and upgrades. Use for operating procedures and readiness with the actual hosting model, recovery objectives and authorized target.

nodes.label: postgresql-performance
nodes.description: Diagnose and improve PostgreSQL query, locking, connection and maintenance performance using representative workload evidence. Use for slow queries, pool pressure, plan regressions and resource bottlenecks.

nodes.label: supabase-postgres-best-practices
nodes.description: Postgres best practices maintained by Supabase, for Postgres running anywhere. Load this skill BEFORE writing or changing anything that lives in a Postgres database: creating or altering tables and columns (including choosing column types), schema design, migrations and declarative schema files, RLS policies and the tests that verify them, indexes, triggers, database functions, queues and scheduled jobs (pg_cron, pgmq), vector/semantic search (pgvector), and restoring dumps (pg_restore) or importing data. Also load it when diagnosing slow queries, high CPU, timeouts, EXPLAIN plans, connection exhaustion, locking, bloat, or rows visible to the wrong user or tenant. This is not just a performance guide — schema, migration, security, and SQL authoring tasks need these rules too, even for a one-column change or a single query.

nodes.label: bash-engineering
nodes.description: Create, refactor and audit reliable Bash CLI utilities, build/operations scripts and CI action entrypoints with safe argument handling, explicit failure semantics, portability, testable side effects and useful documentation.

nodes.label: ci-cd-pipelines
nodes.description: Design or review provider-neutral CI/CD delivery: verification, artifact and deployment stages, artifact identity and promotion, environment and configuration separation, gate design, branching and release flow, recovery, and pipeline evidence. Use when choosing or auditing a pipeline shape rather than implementing a specific provider's syntax.

nodes.label: cli-development
nodes.description: Design or review a command-line application's public surface: command grammar, input precedence, streams and exit codes, interactivity, help and completion, portability, packaging, updates and compatibility. Use when shaping a new CLI or changing an existing one, independent of the implementation language.

nodes.label: github-actions-hardening
nodes.description: Security hardening reviewer for GitHub Actions workflow files (.github/workflows/*.yml). Reasons about the Actions threat model that pattern matchers and general code linters miss — untrusted-input script injection, privileged triggers running fork code, mutable action references, and over-scoped tokens. Use this skill when asked to review, audit, harden, or secure a GitHub Actions workflow, when writing a new workflow, or for any request like "is this workflow safe?", "review my CI for security issues", "why is pull_request_target dangerous here?", "pin my actions", or "lock down GITHUB_TOKEN permissions". Covers script injection via ${{ }} interpolation, pull_request_target / workflow_run privilege escalation, SHA-pinning of third-party actions, least-privilege permissions, GITHUB_ENV/GITHUB_OUTPUT injection, secret exposure, OIDC over long-lived credentials, and self-hosted runner exposure on public repositories.

nodes.label: performance-testing
nodes.description: Design, implement, run or review k6 load and performance checks for application journeys locally, against an application started on a CI runner, or against a deployed non-production environment. Use for latency, concurrency, throughput, saturation and performance regressions; preserve target authority and existing tooling.

nodes.label: playwright-cli
nodes.description: Automate browser interactions, test web pages and work with Playwright tests.

nodes.label: supply-chain-risk-auditor
nodes.description: Audits a project's dependencies for supply-chain risk: version-matched advisories for direct dependencies and the full lockfile tree, abandoned or archived upstreams, npm publisher concentration, and install-time script execution. Use when asked to audit dependencies, assess supply-chain or third-party package risk, or review a dependency tree before an engagement.

nodes.label: tooling-conventions
nodes.description: Configure selected GitHub Actions, Docker/Compose, local quality tools, telemetry backends and web test drivers. Use for their implementation and compatibility details after the project selects those tools; preserve existing alternatives.

nodes.label: explain
nodes.description: Explain a concept to a specific reader so they can predict, apply or decide, using intuition, bounded analogy, mechanism, a worked example, boundary cases and a comprehension check. Use for quick intuition, deep mechanism, decision or code explanation, and correcting a misconception. A conversational craft method, not an artifact contract.

nodes.label: handoff
nodes.description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.

nodes.label: humanizer
nodes.description:
Rewrite AI-sounding text so it reads like the writer without changing what it says.
Use when editing or reviewing prose for AI tells: not-X-but-Y contrasts, one-line
closers, staged openers, forced triads, dashes everywhere, inflated claims, sales
language, stock AI words, bold labels, or filler. Based on Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing."

nodes.label: skill-authoring
nodes.description: Create, revise or review a skill in this collection. Use when adding a capability, deciding between a new skill and an expansion, writing or shortening SKILL.md, choosing references/scripts/assets, defining triggers, composing optional plugins, or evaluating whether a skill changes agent behavior. Not for writing a product document or a one-off prompt.

nodes.label: technical-writing
nodes.description: Cross-type technical writing craft for product and engineering documents, including PRDs, requirements, architecture, decisions, guides and runbooks. Use when reader fit, explanation, structure, examples or presentation need work; artifact contracts, status and homes remain with the artifact system.

nodes.label: writing-for-agents
nodes.description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: design-research
nodes.description: Research shipped products, flows and visual directions before settling an interface decision. Use for competitive and reference research, design benchmarks and pattern evidence; choose sources, separate observation from inference, respect access and privacy limits, and feed material into a comparable option set. Works without paid reference services.

nodes.label: impeccable
nodes.description: Use to design, redesign, critique, audit, polish or animate a frontend: websites, landing pages, dashboards, app UI, components, native iOS/Android screens, or a design system (DESIGN.md).

nodes.label: interface-design
nodes.description: Design, inspect and improve complete user interfaces across navigation, visual hierarchy, behavior, shared composition and accessibility. Use for new UI, cross-screen changes, visual refinements, design reviews and design-to-implementation handoffs; preserve accepted product direction and authorized scope.

nodes.label: testing-journey
nodes.description: Define, automate, explore and evaluate user journeys across web, desktop and mobile applications, including browser extensions. Use for UI/API/persistence changes, interaction and visual consistency, authentication, authorization, lifecycle behavior and failing journey checks.

nodes.label: ui-ux-pro-max
nodes.description: UI/UX design intelligence for web, mobile, and desktop. This skill should be used when designing, building, reviewing, or fixing interfaces, including pages, components, design systems, accessibility, interaction, responsive layout, typography, color, charts, and stack-specific UI implementation. Searchable local data: 80 searchable styles (51 active), 192 product palettes and reasoning profiles, 74 font pairings, 119 UX guidelines, 105 icons, 17 GSAP presets, 25 chart types, and 22 stacks.

nodes.label: usability-research
nodes.description: Plan task-based usability studies and analyze supplied observations for a specific interface or flow. Use for research questions, participant tasks, neutral discussion guides or evidence synthesis; distinguish proposed studies, heuristic review and actual participant findings.

nodes.label: ux-writing
nodes.description: Review, write or harmonize interface labels, instructions, validation, errors, empty states and confirmations in their task context. Use directly for UI copy or during relevant design and implementation; preserve product behavior, established voice, localization and consequential meaning.

nodes.label: native-client-development
nodes.description: Build and verify TypeScript Tauri desktop clients and iOS/Android clients connected to application backends. Use for native shell integration, accepted mobile frameworks, platform lifecycle, secure client storage, packaging and native testing; preserve established client frameworks.

nodes.label: frontend-conventions
nodes.description: Build, extend or review React/Next.js interfaces using the selected component system, compatible styling conventions and supplied visual references. Use for dashboards, customer applications, storefronts, content sites, navigation, styling, forms and frontend architecture; preserve accepted project choices during ordinary feature work.

nodes.label: shadcn
nodes.description: Manages shadcn components and projects — adding, searching, fixing, debugging, styling, and composing UI, including chat interfaces. Provides project context, component docs, and usage examples. Applies when working with shadcn/ui, component registries, presets, --preset codes, or any project with a components.json file. Also triggers for "shadcn init", "create an app with --preset", or "switch to --preset".

nodes.label: tailwind-design-system
nodes.description: Build scalable design systems with Tailwind CSS v4, design tokens, component libraries, and responsive patterns. Use when creating component libraries, implementing design systems, or standardizing UI patterns.

nodes.label: vercel-composition-patterns
nodes.description: React composition patterns that scale. Use when refactoring components with boolean prop proliferation, building flexible component libraries, or designing reusable APIs. Triggers on tasks involving compound components, render props, context providers, or component architecture. Includes React 19 API changes.

nodes.label: vercel-react-best-practices
nodes.description: React and Next.js performance optimization guidelines from Vercel Engineering. This skill should be used when writing, reviewing, or refactoring React/Next.js code to ensure optimal performance patterns. Triggers on tasks involving React components, Next.js pages, data fetching, bundle optimization, or performance improvements.

nodes.label: go-conventions
nodes.description: Build, extend or review Go services, libraries and command-line applications. Use for modules, package/API boundaries, errors, cancellation, runtime lifecycle and meaningful Go verification without requiring a framework.

nodes.label: aks-cost-optimization
nodes.description: Reduce Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) spending: pod rightsizing, VPA-driven recommendations, cluster-autoscaler tuning, spot node pools, namespace-level cost visibility, and cost-anomaly detection. WHEN: rightsize pods, VPA recommendations, idle nodes, scale-down, autoscaler profile, spot nodes, cheaper compute, cost add-on, namespace cost breakdown, spending anomaly, 'my AKS bill is too high', 'is my app consuming what it requests', resource requests vs actual usage, over-provisioned workloads, spot vs on-demand, per-namespace or per-team cost allocation, 'who's spending what and why'. DO NOT USE FOR: GPU / inference cost and idle GPU pools (use aks-gpu-inference); autoscaler that is failing to scale up during an incident (use aks-troubleshooting); choosing SKUs at cluster-creation time (use aks-cluster-setup).

nodes.label: aws-platform
nodes.description: Design, implement or review AWS workloads across identity, network, compute, data, messaging, observability, cost, continuity and edge security. Use for IAM, VPC, ECS/EKS/Lambda, RDS/Aurora, S3, SQS/SNS, CloudWatch, budgets, Backup, Route 53, WAF and Secrets Manager decisions; verify service detail against current AWS docs.

nodes.label: infra-delivery
nodes.description: Define and deliver infrastructure and platform configuration as reconciled desired state across Kubernetes and cloud targets. Use for infrastructure-as-code choice, repository structure, environment promotion, policy and rendered-state validation, Argo CD/Flux GitOps reconciliation, drift, pruning and recovery.

nodes.label: infra-jvm-optimization
nodes.description: Measure and improve application/infrastructure resource efficiency, JVM memory and GC, startup/shutdown, autoscaling, scheduling and resilience during setup, feature changes or recurring optimization reviews.

nodes.label: kubernetes-resource-engineering
nodes.description: Design, generate, review and maintain Kubernetes application/infrastructure resources, Helm charts and Kustomize overlays with secure defaults, reliable lifecycle, controller ownership and rendered validation.

nodes.label: kubernetes-troubleshooting
nodes.description: Diagnose a running Kubernetes workload or cluster problem from observed state. Use for pod lifecycle, events, current and previous logs, probes, resources and scheduling, DNS and Service endpoints, network policy, storage, and control-plane or managed-cluster differences. It does not provision clusters or design manifests.

nodes.label: saas-billing
nodes.description: Design or assess SaaS commercial state, entitlements and billing-provider integration. Use for plans, prices, trials, upgrades, dunning, cancellation, refunds, tax and the event, reconciliation and entitlement contracts behind paid access. Independently of a particular provider except where the platform selects one.

nodes.label: saas-dashboard-design
nodes.description: Design or improve SaaS customer and operator dashboards around decisions, tenant context and actionable workflows. Use for dashboard information architecture, metrics, tables, administration and realistic interface states across frontend stacks.

nodes.label: saas-design
nodes.description: Design or evolve SaaS tenancy, organization/customer lifecycle and administration independently of framework or billing provider. Use when hosted-product behavior crosses identity, commercial and operating boundaries. Entitlement state and commercial mechanics belong to saas-billing.

nodes.label: saas-identity-and-access
nodes.description: Design or assess SaaS organization authority beyond basic authentication, including membership, roles, invitations, ownership transfer, SSO/SCIM, machine identity, support access, tenant isolation and revocation. Use when hosted-product access crosses organizations, enterprise customers or operational staff.

nodes.label: saas-readiness
nodes.description: Assess a SaaS launch, customer rollout or capability expansion against actual commitments and operating evidence. Use for a scoped readiness verdict and prioritized gaps, without assuming every enterprise feature or authorizing release.

nodes.label: saas-supporting-services
nodes.description: Select, integrate and assess the supporting services a hosted product depends on, including analytics, email, observability, hosting and edge, marketing and social automation, search, queues, notifications and support. Use for requirement-first build, buy, adopt or defer decisions and the integration contract, independently of particular vendors.

nodes.label: activity-system
nodes.description: Route development work across activities, stopping points and supporting methods. Use to choose what activity applies, what it produces, where it stops, what may follow, and which artifact or method to use.

nodes.label: analyze-capacity-cost
nodes.description: Analyze measured capacity and cost — demand and saturation, sizing, unit economics, FinOps allocation, forecasting, optimization evidence and verification. Use for a measured review of an existing or proposed system; capacity and cost plans, targets and accepted tradeoffs belong to design-system and the requirements record.

nodes.label: application-configuration
nodes.description: Own the application configuration contract: how an application loads, validates and changes configuration and secrets across local, CI and production targets. Use for source precedence, typed settings, environment parity, runtime reload, multi-tenant defaults, feature-flag boundaries and secret-consumption failure behavior. Credential custody and target delivery remain with their owners.

nodes.label: artifact-system
nodes.description: Maintain engineering artifacts across intent, change, system knowledge, implementation, delivery and entry planes. Use to choose an artifact type, resolve its home, apply its contract and quality bar, and check cross-artifact consistency.

nodes.label: code-review
nodes.description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".

nodes.label: codebase-design
nodes.description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

nodes.label: design
nodes.description: Design UI interactions, backend contracts, AI behavior or architecture for a requested change before implementation. Use when the user wants to settle a solution, compare directions or review a proposal, including a continuation of an exploratory conversation. Use for consequential design alternatives; produce options, type-appropriate linked artifacts and a recorded decision.

nodes.label: design-security
nodes.description: Design security into a feature or system boundary — trust boundaries, data flow, authority placement, privacy, delegation and abuse resistance, including authentication, sessions, federation, machine identity and tenant/resource access. Use when a change introduces identities, user data, external inputs, integrations or new authority; not for scoped remediation, credential operations or compliance assessment.

nodes.label: design-system
nodes.description: Design a system's architecture and tactical system design from product outcomes, existing system evidence and operating constraints. Use after product refinement for a new system, or before planning a feature that changes service, data, client or integration boundaries. Choose strategic structure for hard-to-reverse decisions and a concrete blueprint for runtime shape; this is not a UI component library.

nodes.label: develop
nodes.description: Take a rough business idea, feature, refactor or improvement through clarification, design, implementation, testing and review in one requested engagement. Use when the user asks to build a feature, including after a discussion of its requirements or design. Reuse agreed decisions and fill only gaps needed to implement safely.

nodes.label: diagnosing-bugs
nodes.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.

nodes.label: domain-modeling
nodes.description: Sharpen a project's domain language while designing. Use when terms are overloaded or inconsistent, boundaries are unclear, or a resolved term or consequential choice needs a glossary entry or decision record.

nodes.label: fix
nodes.description: Investigate and repair reported incorrect software behavior when the user asks for a fix. Compare observed behavior with intent, reproduce the defect, apply a focused repair, verify it and hand off the evidence. Use for local or authorized engineering repair after an incident.

nodes.label: git-contributions
nodes.description: Develop a feature in an isolated Git worktree, make Conventional Commits and publish a concise pull request to the correct repository. Apply by default when starting feature work, continuing a feature branch, committing changes or preparing a PR; respect plan-only requests and existing contribution conventions.

nodes.label: grill-me
nodes.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.

nodes.label: grill-with-docs
nodes.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.

nodes.label: grilling
nodes.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

nodes.label: guide-adr
nodes.description: Guide to writing an architecture or product decision record. Covers context, options, decision, consequences, status and supersession.

nodes.label: guide-architecture-views
nodes.description: Guide to producing and reviewing C4 and sequence views. Use for system boundaries, actors, responsibilities, directed dependencies, current versus proposed state, request ordering, synchronous versus asynchronous work, failure, retry, recovery and text equivalents.

nodes.label: guide-assurance-assessment
nodes.description: Guide to writing a scoped assurance assessment. Covers applicability, service boundary, controls, evidence, gaps, disposition and ownership.

nodes.label: guide-compatibility-matrix
nodes.description: Guide to producing and reviewing a compatibility matrix. Use for public surfaces, versions, platforms, runtimes, deprecation, migration and consumer evidence across libraries, CLIs and APIs.

nodes.label: guide-data-model
nodes.description: Guide to documenting a logical data model. Covers entities and relationships, ownership, identity and keys, lifecycle, invariants, consistency, retention, access and tenancy, compatibility, evidence and open decisions.

nodes.label: guide-design-proposal
nodes.description: Guide to writing a design proposal. Covers the decision, constraints, affected components, materially different options, linked artifacts, tradeoffs, seam and recommendation.

nodes.label: guide-design-spec
nodes.description: Guide to producing a design specification that implementation can build and verify from. Covers flows, wireframes, mockups, prototypes, states, content, components, responsiveness, accessibility, motion, assets, handoff and design QA.

nodes.label: guide-ecr
nodes.description: Guide to writing an Engineering Change Record. Covers overview, problem, requirements, solution design, implementation, verification and decisions across a change.

nodes.label: guide-incident-record
nodes.description: Guide to writing an incident record. Covers impact, severity, ownership, timeline, mitigation, recovery verification, current state and follow-up.

nodes.label: guide-issue
nodes.description: Guide to writing an actionable issue. Covers context, intended outcome, scope, acceptance, constraints, verification, dependencies and ownership.

nodes.label: guide-postmortem
nodes.description: Guide to writing a blameless postmortem. Covers timeline, contributing conditions, what worked, actions, owners, verification and open questions.

nodes.label: guide-pr
nodes.description: Guide to writing a pull request description. Covers why, what changed, design impact, validation, risk, release and reviewer links.

nodes.label: guide-prd
nodes.description: Guide to writing a product brief or PRD. Covers problem, audience, outcome, scope, success signal, constraints, evidence and open decisions.

nodes.label: guide-product-feedback-analysis
nodes.description: Guide to writing a product feedback analysis. Covers the decision question, scope, evidence limits, said versus did, findings, competing explanations, implications and open gaps.

nodes.label: guide-readme
nodes.description: Guide to writing a repository README. Covers purpose, audience, quickstart, what it does, open-source adoption, honest claims, docs map, development, support, status and limits.

nodes.label: guide-release-note
nodes.description: Guide to writing a release note or changelog. Covers what shipped, target, changes, migration, compatibility, verification and rollback.

nodes.label: guide-research-report
nodes.description: Guide to writing a decision-oriented research report. Covers question, recommendation, evidence, alternatives, limits and open decision.

nodes.label: guide-rfc
nodes.description: Guide to writing a request for comments or technical proposal. Covers problem, current state, affected components, proposal, alternatives, impact and open decision.

nodes.label: guide-roadmap
nodes.description: Guide to writing and reviewing a strategic or product roadmap. Covers outcomes and evidence, Now/Next/Later horizons, confidence, dependencies, capacity, sequencing, explicit deferrals, status, review cadence and common failures.

nodes.label: guide-runbook
nodes.description: Guide to authoring, exercising and auditing operational runbooks. Covers triggers, prerequisites, diagnosis, mitigation, verification, escalation, recovery, artifact craft and exercise evidence; invoke from design, release, incident response, recovery and operations review as well as runbook maintenance.

nodes.label: guide-state-machine
nodes.description: Guide to producing and reviewing state machines. Use for states, triggers, guards, terminal states, denied transitions, invariants and concurrent or retried behavior.

nodes.label: guide-system-documentation
nodes.description: Guide to discovering, tracing, creating and reviewing the current-system architecture set. Covers evidence, boundaries, responsibilities, runtime behavior, interfaces, deployment, current versus proposed state and document quality.

nodes.label: harden
nodes.description: Assess and address security/privacy weaknesses in the supplied feature, diff or repository. Use for a scoped hardening task with evidence-backed fixes and verification, preserving accepted architecture and task authority.

nodes.label: implement
nodes.description: Implement an agreed change in small verified increments. Use when the work is ready to build, whether the client provides slash commands and a Git flow or only local files and tests.

nodes.label: improve
nodes.description: Assess codebase improvement opportunities or implement a specified improvement objective. Use for architecture, performance, reliability, testability, UX consistency or developer-experience work; bare invocation discovers prioritized evidence-backed opportunities.

nodes.label: plan
nodes.description: Decide whether and what to pursue for a feature, structural change, product area or new application. Use when discussion turns to what to ship first, what is in scope, whether it is feasible, or how to sequence and coordinate multiple changes.

nodes.label: product-direction
nodes.description: Set product direction from user problems, evidence and constraints. Use for discovery, prioritization, useful first slices, success measures and product sequencing before development or when new evidence changes priorities; reuse accepted decisions for defined changes.

nodes.label: project-conventions
nodes.description: Establish or maintain an application repository's structure, stack constraints, repository instruction files for coding agents, local setup and delivery conventions. Use when starting, organizing or reviewing a project, or when repository guidance, commands or agent instructions need to be created, audited or updated; keep ordinary feature work within existing conventions.

nodes.label: prototype
nodes.description: Build a throwaway probe that answers one design question about logic, state or a user interface. Use when design validation needs observed behavior or a rendered choice, not more discussion.

nodes.label: refine
nodes.description: Refine a rough idea, brief, conversation or optional tracker item into repository-aware actionable work. Use to establish scope, acceptance criteria, affected UX/API/data boundaries and material questions before implementation, including when a conversation moves from ideation to defining an actionable feature without authorizing code.

nodes.label: release
nodes.description: Prepare, review or verify an application release or deployment, whether merge-triggered continuous deployment or an explicitly authorized target action. Use for release readiness, post-rollout verification or an authorized target action; bare invocation prepares and reports rather than deploying.

nodes.label: requirements-engineering
nodes.description: Elicit, analyze, validate and maintain verifiable functional and quality requirements for features, refactors, new systems and architecture changes. Use as supporting expertise during refine when stakeholder needs, behavior, cross-system constraints or acceptance are materially uncertain.

nodes.label: research
nodes.description: Investigate a question against primary sources and return traceable findings. Use when facts or behavior must be verified before a planning, refinement or design decision, or when reading work is delegated to a background agent.

nodes.label: retro
nodes.description: Review a session for durable improvements to instructions, checks, navigation and tool economy. Use when asked what should change so future runs need less correction. Stops at candidates; applying them is separately authorized.

nodes.label: run-compliance-assessment
nodes.description: Run a scoped assurance assessment of applicable legal, contractual and privacy requirements — establish applicability and boundary, map controls to owners and evidence, and record gaps, disposition and unclaimed scope. Use for GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, SOC 2 or SaaS subprocessor, residency, export and deletion evidence; it does not certify the service or replace legal or audit judgment.

nodes.label: run-dependency-maintenance
nodes.description: Run dependency and runtime maintenance: review updates, compatibility, release notes and dependent code paths, and handle dependency-update pull requests with CI evidence. Use for explicit or configured maintenance jobs; auto-merge only under an established eligible-update policy. Not for vulnerability triage or general supply-chain audit.

nodes.label: run-incident-response
nodes.description: Coordinate and investigate active service incidents using impact-led triage, reversible stabilization, causal evidence, escalation, communication and independent recovery verification. Use for live or authorized unattended response, not readiness exercises, recurring review or durable repair.

nodes.label: run-operations-review
nodes.description: Plan and run recurring operational reviews of capacity, artifact retention, backup activity, dependency queues, expiring access, scheduled environments, and runbook ownership.

nodes.label: run-postmortem
nodes.description: Facilitate and follow up an incident postmortem: reconstruct evidence, analyse causes and response, derive testable learning actions, and verify that the controls actually work.

nodes.label: run-product-feedback-analysis
nodes.description: Analyze existing user feedback and product usage evidence to evaluate outcomes, identify friction and unmet needs, and inform the next product decision. Use when reviewing a shipped feature, investigating adoption or usability, or prioritizing from available evidence; do not start surveys, contact users or install analytics without a request.

nodes.label: run-production-readiness-review
nodes.description: Run a scoped production-readiness review of whether a service, launch or material capability change is ready to be depended on. Assess reliability and SLOs, observability and alerts, security and authority, capacity and failure behavior, recovery and rollback, runbooks, on-call and support, and open limits. Do not authorize a release or certify the service.

nodes.label: run-security-maintenance
nodes.description: Run credential lifecycle and vulnerability remediation operations — inventory, issue, rotate, revoke and retire credentials, and triage, remediate and verify findings across dependencies, images, infrastructure and deployed targets.

nodes.label: setup
nodes.description: Establish a new application or adopt an existing repository, discover working commands and accepted constraints, and prepare a useful first slice. Use for explicit project setup or adoption; preserve an existing project layout and tooling.

nodes.label: tdd
nodes.description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

nodes.label: test
nodes.description: Select, add, run and review checks; establish completion evidence for a change, journey, component or application. Use as part of implementation or the in-review step, or for an explicit verification request, within the authorized target scope.

nodes.label: testing-resilience
nodes.description: Design, implement, run or review controlled failure tests for application journeys, dependency outages, delays, worker loss and resource exhaustion. Use to verify bounded failure handling and recovery in an authorized isolated or non-production target; choose proportionate fixtures or experiments without requiring a chaos platform.

nodes.label: to-questionnaire
nodes.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.

nodes.label: write-spec
nodes.description: Turn an existing conversation, decision or brief into specification content using the ECR problem, requirements and acceptance structure. Use inside refine to synthesize what is already decided, ask only behavior-changing gaps and leave readiness and publication with the owning activity.

nodes.label: build-strategic-roadmap
nodes.description: Turn an accepted strategy into a bounded operating period: observable outcomes, strategic initiatives, OKRs, capacity, dependencies, cadence and decision rights. Use after the strategy is accepted; stop before the product roadmap, PRD, feature sequencing or delivery commitments.

nodes.label: business-strategy
nodes.description: Develop, evaluate, compare, and continuously update business and product strategy from first principles. Use for startup ideas, business plans, market entry, wedge/beachhead selection, positioning, competitive analysis, economic power and value capture, market structure, customer behavior and culture, future-market scenarios, TAM/SAM/SOM, pricing, go-to-market, monetization, open-source commercialization, unit economics, moats, strategic control points, revenue scenarios, valuation, named strategy frameworks, or when the user wants to determine what a product or company should become. Treat the user's initial concept as a hypothesis, not the strategy.

nodes.label: craft-competitive-analysis
nodes.description: Craft and review competitive analysis: choose the competitor set, profile each rival, project trajectory, assess bundle and platform risk and model likely responses. Use inside a market scan, positioning or strategy engagement; competitive analysis is a mode within strategy, not a separate skill.

nodes.label: craft-strategy-brief
nodes.description: Craft and review a strategy brief: the current thesis, integrated choices, alternatives, assumptions, economics, durability, tripwires and decision history. Use when writing, revising or critiquing a strategy brief or when a proposed strategy must become a durable record.

nodes.label: define-positioning
nodes.description: Decide who the offer is for, what it is compared with, why the customer should switch and why the claim is credible. Use for positioning, category, value proposition and differentiation work; return a defensible argument with proof gaps and exclusions, not marketing copy.

nodes.label: design-business-model
nodes.description: Decide how the business captures value: who pays, for what outcome, on what metric, at what packaging, with what unit economics and what makes the position durable. Use for business model, pricing, packaging and monetization questions; stop before the full financial plan or launch.

nodes.label: discover-customers
nodes.description: Establish how a target customer behaves today, what the status quo costs and where a new choice would fit. Use for interviews, workflow reconstruction, ICP and jobs-to-be-done work before demand or pricing claims; do not invent personas or treat interest as demand.

nodes.label: model-finances
nodes.description: Build a driver-based financial model for a strategy or business model: revenue drivers, cost structure, unit economics, runway and conservative/base/upside plus strategic-downside scenarios. Use for planning, sensitivity and what-must-be-true questions; not for valuation opinions or fundraising process.

nodes.label: plan-go-to-market
nodes.description: Design a repeatable route to the chosen customer: motion, channels, launch sequence, growth loop, funnel metrics and a bounded first plan. Use for launch planning, channel choice and motion changes; stop before product scope or delivery commitments.

nodes.label: raise-capital
nodes.description: Prepare a fundraise around a specific milestone: readiness, round size from the cash model, instrument trade-offs, investor pipeline, data room and runway. Use when deciding whether and how much to raise; do not give legal or tax advice or contact investors without authorization.

nodes.label: review-strategy
nodes.description: Re-test an existing strategy against new evidence and decide continue, narrow, park, pivot or kill. Use for scheduled strategy reviews, fired tripwires and red-team challenges; produce a recorded verdict, not a status meeting.

nodes.label: run-market-scan
nodes.description: Scan a market, segment, competitor set or trend to a decision-relevant depth. Use for entry questions, landscape reviews and competitor profiles; return the strategic implication and gaps, not a feature matrix or a data dump.

nodes.label: set-strategy
nodes.description: Commit to one integrated strategy from competing options. Frame the decision, compare at least three materially different choices, state the cascade, exclusions, economics, falsifiers and opportunity cost, and produce an accepted or explicitly proposed strategy brief.

nodes.label: test-assumptions
nodes.description: Design and interpret experiments that buy a specific decision: tie each test to an assumption, precommit the bar, grade the evidence and choose persevere, narrow, repackage, pivot, park or stop. Use when a live thesis needs behavioural evidence; use validate-idea for premise triage.

nodes.label: validate-idea
nodes.description: Decide whether an early business idea deserves more investment. Challenge the premise, inventory existing evidence, map the decisive assumptions and return go, investigate or stop; use before interviews, pilots or build work, since this activity runs no experiments.

nodes.label: typescript-conventions
nodes.description: Build, extend or review TypeScript libraries, services and clients using the accepted runtime and toolchain. Use for module/compiler configuration, public types, runtime boundaries, package compatibility and meaningful verification independently of a frontend framework.

nodes.label: architecture-diagramming
nodes.description: Create or refine responsive, theme-aware HTML architecture diagrams for structural, runtime, data and deployment explanations. Use when a portable HTML diagram is requested or chosen; preserve existing notation and accepted visual direction.

nodes.label: presentation-building
nodes.description: Create or refine portable single-file HTML slide decks, including narrative, visual direction, responsive/fullscreen layout and optional timeline navigation. Use for HTML presentation work; preserve requested formats and existing deck identity.

nodes.label: system-flow-explorer
nodes.description: Build an explorable, standalone HTML architecture and message-flow explorer from repository evidence or a proposed design. Use when users want to explore a service or repository's architecture, capabilities, dataflow, request lifecycle, sequence messages, or C4 context/container/component views; also use for brainstorming and refining proposed system designs with these views. Keep user scenarios, diagram views, and architecture depth separate. Not for unrelated UI design, generic charts, or application feature implementation.

nodes.label: design-proposal
nodes.home: ECR section, RFC or linked design record

nodes.label: design-specification
nodes.home: design workspace or application design docs

nodes.label: c4-view
nodes.home: architecture set or proposed design record

nodes.label: sequence-view
nodes.home: architecture set or proposed design record
